newsitem.title: UK: LME settles back at close, takes stock of rally.
newsitem.headline: LME settles back at close, takes stock of rally.

text.p: Base metal prices settled back during late Friday LME trading, as the complex paused for breath after a week of considerable gains in some contracts.

Traders said there was profit-taking and technical selling circulating, but the general tone remained upbeat. Investment fund interest was still evident, with further speculative buying lifting zinc to a fresh high for the current move.

Copper forward prices again struggled on the upside and once more showed little inclination to test the $2,280 level. However, attention was centred on the spreads, with tightness resulting in increased backwardations.
The cash/February premium rose to $144/150 from $120 earlier, while cash/threes was at a $205/15 backwardation against $175/180 yesterday.
The major shorts, said to be speculative, were located between the end of January and the first week of February.
"My guess is it's going to get tighter before it gets easier," one trader said.
Last three months business, meanwhile, was at an unchanged $2,248 a tonne.
Meanwhile zinc settled back from the morning's fresh 23-month peaks of $1,147, but still closed at a firmer $1,137, up $17.
Traders said zinc's strength today, in the face of a smaller than expected stock decline of 975 tonnes, was another indication of current bullish sentiment.
Nickel prices were weighed down by a whopping 1,872-tonne increase in LME stocks, although the market proved to be fairly resilient given strength elsewhere. Last trade was at $7,360, down $20.
Lead remained comfortable below yesterday's peaks, closing at $716, up $6. Another upside foray towards the $725 chart level is expected soon, traders said.
Aluminium was somewhat subdued and failed to re-test the eight-month $1,625 peak where it stalled three times this week. Last business was at an unchanged $1,607.
Prices are expected to consolidate at $1,600-$1,625/30 prior to gathering steam for another charge higher towards next resistance at $1,680.
Tin finished at $6,050, up $65, recovering well from lows under $6,000 after retracing from a peak of $6,130 on Thursday. Alloy concluded at $1,508, versus $1,510/12 yesterday.
